text:
Devon: quick idea i wanted to throw out — what if we support an overlay-first bundle format: base weights + small "patch" archives that can be streamed and applied on top. goal: avoid full shard swaps for tiny fixes and enable fast rollouts with atomic commit.

Maria: overlay-first? sounds like a delta-updates approach. how do you see warmup and inference interacting with partially-applied patches?

Devon: two cheap modes: 1) overlay-apply: stream patch zip, map contained safetensors or tensor deltas to in-memory overlay pages; runtime serves using base+overlay lookup (overlay wins). 2) fallback-materialize: download then synthesize a new full shard file and swap. overlay-apply lets us serve unchanged layers immediately.

Alex: i'd prefer we don't change the sharded safetensors binary format. can patches be packaged as tiny safetensors files (per-tensor) and the loader just maps them into an overlay namespace?

Devon: exactly. patch zip contains entries like embeddings.safetensors, block_3.weight.safetensors. Manifest indicates mapping: scope -> patch_id -> apply_strategy (overlay|replace).

Sam: atomicity concern: if a sequence of patches is being applied and commit fails mid-way we must not leave a corrupt runtime. proposals?

Devon: handshake proposal: 1) GET /bundle/<id>/manifest returns manifest + compatible shard-map 2) client downloads base if needed (with range support) 3) client streams patch files via /bundle/<id>/patches/<patch_id> and writes overlay pages to transient overlay store 4) client POST /bundle/<id>/commit -> runtime verifies final checksum manifest (base+patches) then atomically flips active pointer to include overlay references. If commit fails runtime discards overlay or quarantines it for bg-retry.

Alex: add a lease/timestamp on overlay resources so stale in-progress overlays get GC'd. Also limit concurrent patch downloads per node to protect IO.

Maria: warmup/readiness implications: router needs per-shard per-scope readiness. propose runtime exposes a simple readiness map: tensor-scope -> state (ready|partial|missing). Router uses this to route cold prefixes to fallback model/region.

Devon: sample readiness header we can return from /runtime/health:
X-Bundle-Readiness: embeddings=ready,blocks.0-7=partial,head=ready

Sam: rollback approach: quarantine on failed commit + metrics. keep overlay but mark it non-serving until repaired so we can debug. but need eviction path to reclaim memory.

Alex: compatibility with existing signed manifests: patches must be referenced in signed manifest and the manifest signature must cover patch digests. don't allow unsigned ad-hoc patches.

Maria: perf experiment idea: one tenant, base=8GB, embedding-patch=250MB. test overlay vs full-swap latency, peak mem, and apply duration. also measure cold-start correctness when overlay arrives mid-inflight.

Devon: good. metrics to add: patch_apply_duration_ms, overlay_mem_bytes, failed_commit_count, overlay_quarantine_count. also tracing spans for patch-download and checksum-verify.

Sam: security note: ensure patch zips can't reference unexpected scopes (restrict regex), and verify file-level checksums. signed manifest + per-patch signature preferable.

Alex: loader changes summary: - preserve current safetensors shard layout - add overlay namespace lookup (overlay takes precedence) - commit API to atomically swap pointer - rollback/quarantine API and lease GC

Devon: router changes summary: - read readiness map from runtime - fallback rules: if crucial scope is partial -> route to base-only variant or fallback region - optionally send probe requests to warmup in parallel

Maria: can we stage rollout by scope? e.g. first apply embeddings patch only to a subset of replicas to monitor quality then roll globally. need rollout metadata in manifest (canary percentage).

Devon: i'll add canary metadata: patches[] entries can include rollout: {type:percent, value:10} and runtime enforces placement.

deploy-bot: Link: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/overlay-bundles (draft created by Devon)

Sam: +1. small ask: put explicit limits on overlay memory per-replica and per-tenant, and a backpressure mechanism when overlay apply hits IO limit.

Devon: will include in RFC. next steps: i'll write a short RFC with handshake state machine, manifest extension, loader change list, router readiness map, safety/lease rules, and PoC perf plan. thanks all. :shipit:

Maria: react :thumbsup:
